refsection.title: Description
refsection.para: The GmatFunction resource declares a new GMAT function or can be used to load-in a pre-existing GMAT function. This function can be called in the Mission Sequence through GMAT's CallGmatFunction command. See the reference for details.

Through this GMAT function, data can be passed in the function as input and received as output. Data that is passed into the function as input or received from the function as output can also be declared as global. See the reference for more details. See also the and sections for detailed discussion on GMAT functions and how to use them.

Changes to a hardware definition during a GMAT function notify spacecraft attachments derived from that actual definition. Separate resources with the same name remain independent. Function value copies map attachment relationships into their copied resource graph, while explicit globals retain shared relationships. Fresh local declaration graphs are associated after their declaration values are complete.
See Also: ,

Simulator and TrackingFileSet values disclose their native owned definitions to the function context. Copied tracking filters, participant references and propagation assignments bind to their corresponding private or caller objects. Binding does not start simulation or open data streams; estimator and smoother values use the same owned-component binding contract.

BatchEstimator, ExtendedKalmanFilter and Smoother provide native function-value bindings for their owned definitions, estimation-state declarations and retained restoration snapshots. Values remain dormant until native command preparation; copying does not resume a running estimation session or open its observation files.

ContactLocator, EclipseLocator and IntrusionLocator values bind their target, observer, occulting-body, sensor and other native references to the corresponding caller objects or private function-value copies. Contact additional-target workers retain their native owned results. Copying keeps event results as values and leaves the locator dormant; the next native search prepares its runtime. Open reports, active ephemeris-manager sessions and generated instrument kernels are not transferred as running sessions.

PlanetographicRegion values copy their latitude/longitude definition, input filename and calculated polygon vertices. Body references and frames bind separately. Native initialization reuses a completed polygon; an unprepared definition follows the ordinary polygon preparation path.

A retained resource graph can include a private EphemerisFile dependency. Its spacecraft, frame, model and wrapper references bind in the same graph. The private ephemeris refers back to that graph without owning it; a detached native copy can retain the graph while its references are rebound, including a reference back to the original public root. Detaching an interior value requires that root to remain alive while it is captured; incompatible native ownership layouts still report an error. Copying does not transfer an open writer, accepted output history or a running ephemeris session.

Captured estimation restoration destinations are rebound by actual object identity when snapshot values move between scopes. Restoring values preserves destination resource names and does not use an equal name to substitute another resource. Capture restoration buffers through the native estimation state manager before supplying them to a smoother.
Saved station values keep their hardware and error-model references within the corresponding function or caller scope. Restoring those values preserves the configured component names and references.

Spacecraft values disclose their owned components to the function context. Saved estimation values keep the selected spacecraft components and environment references when restored within a compatible run.

entry.para: Allows the user to define a valid function path. In the GUI, the FunctionPath field is activated after editing the function and then clicking on the function's Save As button. The path of the function can be defined as either absolute or relative.

listitem.para: Valid file path. The path can be either absolute or relative. In the Script mode, if this field is not used at all, then default location of functions is GMAT's ...\userfunctions\gmat\ directory

refsection.title: Source format compatibility
refsection.para: SourceFormat = Native is the default and retains the native function parser's filename and encoding policy. The Qt file editor uses UTF-8. Select SourceFormat = LegacyASCII to require a resolved function filename ending in .gmf and seven-bit ASCII bytes throughout its contents, including comments. Non-ASCII bytes, including a UTF-8 byte order mark, produce an error with a byte offset. Source fragments loaded with #Include must also end in .gmf and pass the ASCII check. In Native mode, include fragments can have other filenames. Nested function resources select their own policy.

The SourceFormat field is available in the Qt resource editor and in resource assignments before the mission sequence. It is not a mission command setting. Rebuild a function before changing its policy after its source has been interpreted. A compiled function must also be rebuilt before changing its resolved FunctionPath; assigning a new path cannot relabel its cached command sequence. Editing or saving a source file does not certify that it satisfies the selected policy; the parser enforces the policy when building the function.

Function-resource copies follow the same rebuild rule. Copying an identical file/source/call policy into a compiled function retains its compiled interface and current invocation state. Assigning a different definition to that compiled resource requires rebuilding it first. An uncompiled destination receives the definition with fresh execution state; command sequences, local prototypes and runtime bindings are not borrowed from the source function.

FunctionPath accepts a function file or a directory. Relative paths are resolved against the GMAT script working directory; an existing match in the binary directory is used as a fallback. Existing directories and paths ending in a path separator are treated as directories, including directories whose names contain .gmf. A directory receives the resource's function name and .gmf suffix. Empty paths are rejected.

A GroundStation passed as an input is a local value, including its station-owned hardware and error models. Include the formal argument in the output list to copy its changed value back to the caller. Objects explicitly accessed as Global retain their shared identity.

Estimator and simulator resource copies retain separate owned propagation definitions and their actual source relationships. Their measurement managers use the copied resource's propagation list. This commands stage related propagation, tracking and filter definition changes and rebuild their native engines when execution next reaches the command. Measurement managers own tracking/filter copies and rebuild generated adapters. Independent participant, hardware and navigation-state value graphs retain their separate resource-specific requirements.

Native propagation commands and Target/Optimize solver commands also track their actual engine definitions for clone updates. Nested propagator and force-model changes reach the containing propagation command. Copied snapshots remain inactive, and commands release their update subscriptions when their function bindings are retired. Estimator and simulator commands apply related definition updates at their next execution boundary, preserving delayed observation initialization.

RequireOutputBrackets = false (default) retains the native single-output shorthand for standalone function-call commands. Select RequireOutputBrackets = true to require square brackets around the output list, including one output: [result] = MyFunction(input);. The native parser and initialized call commands enforce this setting using the original call syntax, even if serialization has subsequently added brackets. A scalar assignment whose entire right-hand side is a GMAT function call is also subject to this rule. Set this resource field before the mission sequence; it is also available in the Qt resource editor. A call that assigns no outputs retains its existing syntax, such as MyFunction(input); or MyFunction(); for a function with no inputs. It does not need an output list, and normal argument-count validation still applies. Conversion of single-output shorthand into a call command preserves the authored bracket choice for validation; canonical serialization does not make an unbracketed call satisfy the strict setting. Expressions that combine a function result with other calculations retain native expression syntax.

refsection.title: GUI
refsection.para: In the GUI, a new GmatFunction resource is created as follows:

listitem.para: In the Resources Tree, right click on the Functions folder, select Add -> GMAT Function -> New
In the New GMAT function dialog box, type the desired name of your function.

refsection.para: The GmatFunction resource's GUI window is very simple. When a new GMAT function is created through the GUI, the FunctionPath field is defined by first editing the function and then clicking on the Save As button. This lets you graphically define the path.

refsection.title: Remarks
refsection.para: Spacecraft and error-model value copies retain complete covariance values independently of their configured sigma priors. Restoring an unchanged layout retains destination matrix storage and owner bindings. Parameter-block covariance results remain temporary and may be replaced by the next block request.

Force-model native copies disclose their force children and map force-owned solve-for references into the copied components. Detached acceleration-reporting copies continue to exclude transient forces and use their existing reporting policy. Restoration within the same prepared graph retains current force identities and bindings.

Native drag copies own independent numerical buffers and internal atmosphere values. Exponential atmosphere tables and loaded solar-flux data copy as values. Shared external atmospheres remain bound through their owning body; changing a shared atmosphere is distinct from restoring a drag value.

Compatible restoration keeps spacecraft mass-property interpolators and file-thrust interpolation tables in their current storage. Ring-buffer counters, direction and supported scratch values are restored with the data. Their native owners also prepare private caches when presence or supported storage layouts differ from capture, including a spline first created during execution. Other changed resource bindings and Hermite derivative/cache layouts still require native preparation. Ordinary Hermite value copies retain their derivative and polynomial data.

Native physical-model value copies own their state, derivative and optional Jacobian arrays. A separate translated state remains separate in the copy. Restoring values within an unchanged layout retains the destination storage and selected environment bindings; changed force configuration requires preparation.

GMAT function calls inside an optimization sequence continue to execute as GMAT commands. MATLAB optimizer callbacks select the active optimizer service; a Function resource is not a callback service. This routing rule does not change the normal GMAT-to-MATLAB function interface.

A MATLAB function called by GMAT inside a Qt optimizer callback uses the waiting MATLAB client's base workspace. Numeric column order, character data and the existing supported structure/cell representations are retained. Per-callback output buffers and calling names do not replace the outer C Engine call's state. The optimizer protocol continues to accept fixed evaluation requests, rather than a general MATLAB-to-GMAT function-call interface.

Linux Qt MAT-file writers retain independent numeric and string buffers when copied. Diagnostic output inside a function or optimizer callback uses completed file operations rather than sharing a live MATLAB file handle with the enclosing command.

When a GMAT-called MATLAB function is evaluating, external script edits, mission execution and callback execution are rejected. Native GMAT argument evaluation and native function commands retain their normal execution path. After a clear, script edit or failed build/update, the external controller must successfully build the current script before running it.

Object and parameter replies through the MATLAB interface retain complete serialized strings. A sandbox object with the requested name takes precedence over a configured object; a non-Parameter cannot be read through the parameter interface by treating it as a Parameter. Owned string replies and legacy borrowed character adapters have distinct storage lifetimes.

Qt callback workspace scopes preserve known optimizer-driver variables separately from unrelated user variables. They retain whether a base name existed and whether it referred to the global workspace. Restoring a compatible global keeps an existing global binding; a child's newly introduced private bindings are removed. MATLAB handle values retain MATLAB assignment semantics.
If a function call fails, expression evaluation reports an error. It does not substitute the result of an earlier call.

refsection.title: Input and Output Arguments
refsection.para: Arguments can be passed into a GMAT function as input and returned from a GMAT function as output. You can pass GMAT objects as input to a function and receive entire objects as output from the function. If a given GMAT object is not declared as global in both the main script and in the function, then all objects that are passed into or received as output from the function are considered to be local to that function and the main script.

In GMAT, you can use CallGmatFunction command to pass GMAT objects as input arguments and receive objects as output from the function. In general, any objects in GMAT's Resources tree can be passed as input to the function. Most common objects that a user is likely to pass as input to the function are objects that are related to propagating a spacecraft, performing differential correction (DC) in a targeter, implementing optimization in an optimizer loop, user-defined variables/arrays/strings or subscribers that are used to draw or report parameters. Note that similar to most coding languages, if a resource of the same name of an input is created within the function, that object is freshly initialized and the input object's parameters are ignored. Most common objects that are likely to be passed as output arguments from the function maybe a Spacecraft resource or user-defined objects such as Variables, Arrays or Strings.

Below is a list of allowed objects that can be passed as input and output to and from the function. Also see section that show two distinct methods in two separate examples of how to pass local objects as inputs to the function, perform an operation inside the function, then receive local objects as outputs from the function.

The input arguments can be any of the following types:
Any resource objects (e.g. Spacecraft, Propagator, DC, Optimizers, Impulsive or FiniteBurns)
resource parameter of real number type (e.g. Spacecraft.X)
resource parameter of string type (e.g. Spacecraft.UTCGregorian)
Array, String, or Variable resource

The output arguments can be any of the following types:
Resource object like Spacecraft
resource parameter of real number type (e.g. Spacecraft.X)
resource parameter of string type (e.g. Spacecraft.UTCGregorian)
Array, String, or Variable resource

refsection.title: Global Spacecraft, Subscribers and Other Objects
refsection.para: In GMAT, objects can be declared as global by using the Global command in the Mission tree. All default objects present in GMAT's Resources tree or any new user-defined resources can be declared as global. Currently any default or new user-defined coordinate systems, SolarSystemBarycenter, SolarSystem, default or new user-defined propagators are automatic global objects and not needed to be specifically declared as global via the Global command.

Often times, there will be cases when you will propagate a spacecraft both in the main script and from inside the GMAT function. Additionally users may want to report and/or plot spacecraft's trajectory, parameters, variables, arrays and strings to same subscribers both from the main script and/or solely from inside the function. If you want to report and plot continuous set of data to any of the five subscribers (i.e. OrbitView, GroundTrack, XYPlot, ReportFile, EphemerisFile), then always declare your Spacecraft object and subscriber objects as global both in the main script and inside the function. Abiding by this rule draws plots, reports and ephemeris files correctly and flow of data will be reported continuously to all the subscribers.

In general, a good scripting practice is that objects that have been declared global don't need to be sent as input or output arguments to and from the function. For example, if Spacecraft, all subscriber objects or objects that are used to perform propagation, targeting or optimization have already been declared global, then you don't to be redundant and send those global objects again as input or receive them as output from the function. Having said that, GMAT does allow globally declared objects such as Spacecraft, global variables/arrays/strings to be passed as input/output argument to and from the function. Globally declared objects such as spacecraft, variables/arrays/strings can be plotted or reported interchangeably both from the main script and inside the function to globally declared subscribers.

See section that shows three examples of how to declare spacecraft, all five subscribers and variables/arrays as global in both the main script and inside the function. As you run the examples, notice that the flow of data reported to all five subscribers is continuous.

refsection.title: Using GMAT Functions in an Assignment Command
refsection.para: GMAT allows you to use simple GMAT functions in the main script in an assignment command mode. Below example snippet shows how to use simple GMAT functions in mathematical statements. Note that in the below snippet, function path to GMAT function's FunctionPath field was not specifically defined. Whenever the FunctionPath field is not defined in the script mode, then preferred default path of these functions is in the following directory where GMAT was installed: ..GMAT\userfunctions\gmat\

programlisting.code:
%%Using a GMAT function in a mathematical statement
Create ReportFile rf
Create GmatFunction Math_GmatPi Math_GmatSin Create GmatFunction Math_GmatAtan2 Math_GmatInv
Create Variable x y z pi in Create Array A[2,2] B[2,2]
BeginMissionSequence
A(1,1) = 1 A(1,2) = 3 A(2,1) = 4 A(2,2) = 2
% no inputs into the function pi = Math_GmatPi * 2 Report rf pi
% one input into the function [pi] = Math_GmatPi in = pi/4 x = Math_GmatSin(in) - 15 Report rf x
% two inputs: in = 0.5 y = Math_GmatAtan2(in, x)^2 Report rf y
% array input/output: B = Math_GmatInv(A)' Report rf B
%%%% Math_GmatPi Function begins below:
function [pi] = Math_GmatPi Create Variable pi BeginMissionSequence pi = acos(-1)
%%%% Math_GmatSin Function begins below:
function [y] = Math_GmatSin(x) Create Variable y BeginMissionSequence y = sin(x)
%%%% Math_GmatAtan2 Function begins below:
function [z] = Math_GmatAtan2(y, x) Create Variable z BeginMissionSequence z = atan2(y, x)
%%%% Math_GmatInv Function begins below:
function [B] = Math_GmatInv(A) Create Array B[2,2] BeginMissionSequence B = inv(A)

informalexample.para: Method 1 of how to pass local objects into the function and receiving local objects as the output from the function. Pass local spacecraft, other local objects into the function, perform hohmann targeting inside the function, receive updated local spacecraft, local variables as output and finally report them to local subscribers in the main script. Since the spacecraft and all five subscribers were only local objects (i.e. not declared as global), hence notice that all subscribers begin to draw and report data once the updated spacecraft is returned back and propagated in the main script.

Method 2 of how to pass local objects into the function and receiving local objects as the output from the function. In this method, notice that we now only pass local spacecraft as input to the function. Instead of passing additional local objects into the function, we now create those required local objects inside the function itself. Similar to method 1, we perform hohmann targeting inside the function, then send updated spacecraft and variables back to the main script as output from the function. Finally updated spacecraft is propagated for one day in main script and reported by all subscribers. Since the spacecraft and all five subscribers were only local objects (i.e. not declared as global), hence notice that all subscribers begin to draw and report data once the updated spacecraft begins propagation in the main script.

In this example, we declare spacecraft, all subscribers and other objects as global in both main script and in function. Propagate inside the function, perform targeting inside function, and report local variables, global spacecraft state and global variable (DV1, DV2) to global reportfile. Next, we continue to propagate in the main script and continue to report spacecraft state to global reportfile in the main script. After running this example, pay special attention to all subscribers. Note that spacecraft trajectory is plotted continuously on three plotting subscribers and data is reported continuously as well to both reportfiles and ephemerisfile.

programlisting.code:
Create Spacecraft aSat
Create ForceModel aFM aFM.CentralBody = Earth aFM.PointMasses = {Earth}
Create Propagator aProp aProp.FM = aFM
Create ImpulsiveBurn TOI Create ImpulsiveBurn GOI
Create DifferentialCorrector DC
Create OrbitView anOrbitView anOrbitView.SolverIterations = Current anOrbitView.Add = {aSat, Earth}
Create GroundTrack GroundTrack1 GroundTrack1.Add = {aSat} GroundTrack1.CentralBody = Earth
Create XYPlot XYPlot1 XYPlot1.XVariable = aSat.ElapsedDays XYPlot1.YVariables = {aSat.EarthMJ2000Eq.X}
Create ReportFile rf rf.Add = {aSat.UTCGregorian, aSat.EarthMJ2000Eq.X, ... aSat.EarthMJ2000Eq.Y, aSat.EarthMJ2000Eq.Z, ... aSat.EarthMJ2000Eq.VX, aSat.EarthMJ2000Eq.VY, aSat.EarthMJ2000Eq.VZ}
Create ReportFile rf2 rf2.WriteHeaders = false
Create EphemerisFile anEphemerisFile anEphemerisFile.Spacecraft = aSat
Create GmatFunction Global_Subscribers Global_Subscribers.FunctionPath = ... 'C:\Users\rqureshi\Desktop\Global_Subscribers.gmf'
Create Variable DV1 DV2
BeginMissionSequence;
% Declare aSat, Subscribers and other objects as Global: Global aSat Global aFM TOI GOI DC %aProp is global by default. Global anOrbitView GroundTrack1 XYPlot1 rf rf2 anEphemerisFile Global DV1 DV2
Report rf2 aSat.UTCGregorian aSat.UTCModJulian aSat.X aSat.Y aSat.Z ... aSat.VX aSat.VY aSat.VZ
% Call function: Global_Subscribers()
% Report updated Global S/C, TOI and GOI: Report rf2 aSat.UTCGregorian aSat.UTCModJulian aSat.X aSat.Y aSat.Z ... aSat.VX aSat.VY aSat.VZ TOI.Element1 GOI.Element1
Propagate 'Prop one more day' aProp(aSat) {aSat.ElapsedDays = 1.0}
Report rf2 aSat.UTCGregorian aSat.UTCModJulian aSat.X aSat.Y aSat.Z ... aSat.VX aSat.VY aSat.VZ
% Report Global DV1 and DV2 to global 'rf2' in main script: Report rf2 DV1 DV2
%%%%%%%%%%% Function begins below:
function Global_Subscribers()
% Create Local variables, string: Create Variable sc_epoch x y z vx vy vz dv1 dv2; Create String utc_epoch
Global aSat Global aFM TOI GOI DC Global anOrbitView GroundTrack1 XYPlot1 rf rf2 anEphemerisFile Global DV1 DV2
BeginMissionSequence
Propagate 'Propagate to Periapsis' aProp(aSat) {aSat.Earth.Periapsis}
Target 'Hohmann Transfer' DC {SolveMode = Solve, ExitMode = SaveAndContinue} Vary 'Vary TOI' DC(TOI.Element1 = 1.0, {Perturbation = 0.0001, ... Lower = 0.0, Upper = 3.14159, MaxStep = 0.5}) Maneuver 'Perform TOI' TOI(aSat) Propagate 'Prop to Apoapsis' aProp(aSat) {aSat.Earth.Apoapsis} Achieve 'Achieve RMAG = 42165' DC(aSat.Earth.RMAG = 42165) Vary 'Vary GOI' DC(GOI.Element1 = 1.0, {Perturbation = 0.0001, ... Lower = 0.0, Upper = 3.14159, MaxStep = 0.2}) Maneuver 'Perform GOI' GOI(aSat) Achieve 'Achieve ECC = 0.005' DC(aSat.Earth.ECC = 0.005) EndTarget
sc_epoch = aSat.UTCModJulian utc_epoch = aSat.UTCGregorian x = aSat.X y = aSat.Y z = aSat.Z vx = aSat.VX vy = aSat.VY vz = aSat.VZ dv1 = TOI.Element1 dv2 = GOI.Element1
% Report local variables/strings to Global reportfile 'rf2': Report rf2 utc_epoch sc_epoch x y z vx vy vz dv1 dv2
Propagate 'Prop one Day Inside Function' aProp(aSat) {aSat.ElapsedDays = 1.0}
% Report Global aSat state to global 'rf2': Report rf2 aSat.UTCGregorian aSat.UTCModJulian aSat.X aSat.Y aSat.Z aSat.VX ... aSat.VY aSat.VZ TOI.Element1 GOI.Element1
% Report Global variables DV1 and DV2 to global 'rf2' in main script: DV1 = TOI.Element1 DV2 = TOI.Element1

informalexample.para: Just as previous example, we declare spacecraft, all subscribers and other objects as global in both main script and in function. This time GMAT function is nested inside control logic statements like While and If-EndIf. LEO station-keeping is performed inside the function. As the example will be running, pay special attention to all subscribers. Note that spacecraft trajectory is plotted continuously on three plotting subscribers and data is reported continuously as well to both reportfiles and ephemerisfile.

programlisting.code:
Create Spacecraft LEOsat LEOsat.DisplayStateType = Keplerian LEOsat.SMA = 6733.989999999996 LEOsat.ECC = 0.0004329999999984123 LEOsat.INC = 34.98399999999998 LEOsat.RAAN = 274.742 LEOsat.AOP = 287.8049999999732 LEOsat.TA = 294.0690000000269
Create ForceModel LEOprop_ForceModel LEOprop_ForceModel.CentralBody = Earth LEOprop_ForceModel.PrimaryBodies = {Earth} LEOprop_ForceModel.PointMasses = {Luna, Sun} LEOprop_ForceModel.SRP = On LEOprop_ForceModel.GravityField.Earth.Degree = 4 LEOprop_ForceModel.GravityField.Earth.Order = 4 LEOprop_ForceModel.GravityField.Earth.PotentialFile = 'JGM2.cof' LEOprop_ForceModel.Drag.AtmosphereModel = JacchiaRoberts LEOprop_ForceModel.Drag.F107 = 150 LEOprop_ForceModel.Drag.F107A = 150
Create Propagator LEOprop LEOprop.FM = LEOprop_ForceModel
Create ImpulsiveBurn TCM1 Create ImpulsiveBurn TCM2
Create DifferentialCorrector DC
Create OrbitView DefaultOrbitView DefaultOrbitView.Add = {LEOsat, Earth}
Create XYPlot XYPlot1 XYPlot1.XVariable = LEOsat.A1ModJulian XYPlot1.YVariables = {LEOsat.Earth.Altitude}
Create GroundTrack GroundTrack1 GroundTrack1.Add = {LEOsat}
Create ReportFile rf
Create ReportFile rf2 rf2.Add = {LEOsat.UTCModJulian, LEOsat.Earth.Altitude, ... LEOsat.Earth.RMAG, LEOsat.Earth.ECC}
Create EphemerisFile anEphemerisFile anEphemerisFile.Spacecraft = LEOsat
Create GmatFunction TargetLEOStationKeeping TargetLEOStationKeeping.FunctionPath = ... 'C:\Users\rqureshi\Desktop\TargetLEOStationKeeping.gmf'
Create Variable desiredRMAG desiredECC X Y Z
BeginMissionSequence
desiredRMAG = 6737 desiredECC = 0.00005
% Declare LEOsat, Subscribers and other objects as Global: Global LEOsat Global DC TCM1 TCM2 LEOprop_ForceModel Global DefaultOrbitView XYPlot1 GroundTrack1 Global rf rf2 anEphemerisFile
While 'While ElapsedDays < 10' LEOsat.ElapsedDays < 10.0
Propagate 'Prop One Step' LEOprop(LEOsat)
If 'If Alt < Threshold' LEOsat.Earth.Altitude < 342
Propagate 'Prop To Periapsis' LEOprop(LEOsat) {LEOsat.Periapsis}
% Call function to implement SK. Pass local variables as input: TargetLEOStationKeeping(desiredRMAG,desiredECC)
EndIf
EndWhile
Report rf LEOsat.UTCGregorian LEOsat.UTCModJulian LEOsat.X ... LEOsat.Y LEOsat.Z LEOsat.Earth.Altitude LEOsat.Earth.ECC
%%%%%%%%%%% Function begins below:
function TargetLEOStationKeeping(desiredRMAG,desiredECC)
BeginMissionSequence
Global LEOsat Global DC TCM1 TCM2 LEOprop_ForceModel Global DefaultOrbitView XYPlot1 GroundTrack1 Global rf rf2 anEphemerisFile
Target 'Raise Orbit' DC {SolveMode = Solve, ExitMode = DiscardAndContinue} Vary 'Vary TCM1.V' DC(TCM1.Element1 = 0.002, {Perturbation = 0.0001, ... Lower = -9.999999e300, Upper = 9.999999e300, MaxStep = 0.05}) Maneuver 'Apply TCM1' TCM1(LEOsat); Propagate 'Prop to Apoapsis' LEOprop(LEOsat) {LEOsat.Apoapsis} Achieve 'Achieve RMAG' DC(LEOsat.RMAG = desiredRMAG, {Tolerance = 0.1}) Vary 'Vary TCM2.V' DC(TCM2.Element1 = 1e-005, {Perturbation = 0.00005, ... Lower = -9.999999e300, Upper = 9.999999e300, MaxStep = 0.05}) Maneuver 'Apply TCM2' TCM2(LEOsat); Achieve 'Achieve ECC' DC(LEOsat.Earth.ECC = desiredECC) EndTarget

informalexample.para: In this example, all arrays, string and a single subscriber are declared global both in main script and inside function. Note that global arrays are passed into the function, cross products are computed and computed global arrays (v5, v6) are sent back to the main script. Also note that global arrays, string are reported to global report file in both main script and inside the function.

programlisting.code:
Create ReportFile rf rf.WriteHeaders = false
Create GmatFunction cross3by1; cross3by1.FunctionPath = ... 'C:\Users\rqureshi\Desktop\cross3by1.gmf'
Create Array v1[3,1] v2[3,1] v3[3,1] ... v4[3,1] v5[3,1] v6[3,1] Create String tempstring
BeginMissionSequence
% Declare Arrays, string and subscriber as global: Global v1 v2 v3 v4 v5 v6 tempstring rf
v1(1,1) = 1 v1(2,1) = 2 v1(3,1) = 3 v2(1,1) = 4 v2(2,1) = 5 v2(3,1) = 6 v3(1,1) = 8 v3(2,1) = 9 v3(3,1) = 10 v4(1,1) = 10 v4(2,1) = 11 v4(3,1) = 12
% Report global arrays/string to global 'rf': Report rf v1 v2 v3 v4 tempstring = '--------------------' Report rf tempstring
% Call function. Pass in Global arrays % Receive global arrays in return: [v5, v6] = cross3by1(v1, v2, v3, v4)
% Report global output to global 'rf': Report rf v5 v6
tempstring = '--------------------' Report rf tempstring
%%%%%%%%%%% Function begins below:
function [v5, v6] = cross3by1(vector1,vector2, vector3, vector4)
BeginMissionSequence
Global v1 v2 v3 v4 v5 v6 tempstring rf
v5(1,1) = vector1(2,1)*vector2(3,1) - vector1(3,1)*vector2(2,1) v5(2,1) = -(vector1(1,1)*vector2(3,1) - vector1(3,1)*vector2(1,1)) v5(3,1) = vector1(1,1)*vector2(2,1) - vector1(2,1)*vector2(1,1)
v6(1,1) = vector3(2,1)*vector4(3,1) - vector3(3,1)*vector4(2,1) v6(2,1) = -(vector3(1,1)*vector4(3,1) - vector3(3,1)*vector4(1,1)) v6(3,1) = vector3(1,1)*vector4(2,1) - vector3(2,1)*vector4(1,1)
v1 = v1 + 1 v2 = v2*2 v3 = v3/2 v4 = v4 + v4
% Continue to report global arrays/string to global 'rf': Report rf v1 v2 v3 v4 tempstring = '--------------------' Report rf tempstring
